theater: 英吉利海峽與不列顛南部

battle.name: 卡勞修斯的起義
battle.theater: 英吉利海峽與不列顛南部
battle.brief: 公元286年末，海峽艦隊指揮官卡勞修斯被控私吞海盜贓物，拒受審判而舉兵稱帝，控制不列顛與高盧北海岸線達七年。馬克西米安兩次渡海討伐皆因羅馬水師缺乏經驗而失敗，296年康斯坦提烏斯自布洛涅出發，攻城時以扭力投石機對付薩克森海岸的羅馬堡壘，才奪回倫敦與全島。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 起義的一方是不列顛海峽艦隊（Classis Britannica）以及它所控制的不列顛與高盧北海沿岸，實際的權力核心是卡勞修斯在布洛涅（Gesoriacum）與諾維奧杜努姆的兩處基地。他出身高盧北部的梅納皮人地區，可能帶有低羅馬或日耳曼血統，被皇帝任命為艦隊指揮官，負責清剿法蘭克與撒克遜海盜；事後以縱盜劫掠、坐吞贓物的罪名被控告，於是自稱奧古斯都，建立以英格蘭為核心的割據政權：自鑄貨幣、任命財政官阿萊克圖斯，並把高盧北岸一併置於旗下。另一方是羅馬帝國中央，先後由戴克里先與馬克西米安主持：戴克里先在286至293年間推行分權，293年增設「六貴族」委員會，專責處理對卡勞修斯的追訴；296年由凱撒君士坦提烏斯·克洛魯斯率海陸大軍渡海收復全島。帝國一方的部隊由高盧與萊茵的駐軍、輔兵團與重建中的海軍艦隊組成；卡勞修斯一方則以海峽艦隊為骨幹，輔以英國當地徵召的艦上人員、沿岸輔兵，並有法蘭克與撒克森部族以劫掠船隊的方式介入。
countriesEn: The side that rebelled was the Classis Britannica, the Channel fleet, together with Britain and the northern coast of Gaul that it controlled; the real centre of power lay in Carausius's two bases at Gesoriacum (Boulogne) and Noviodunum. He came from the Menapian region of northern Gaul, was possibly of low Roman or Germanic stock, and had been appointed by the emperor to command the fleet with the task of clearing the sea of Frankish and Saxon pirates. When he was accused of letting the pirates raid and then keeping the proceeds for himself, he proclaimed himself Augustus and set up a breakaway state centred on England: he struck his own coinage, appointed a finance minister, Allectus, and brought the northern shore of Gaul under his rule as well. The other side was the Roman imperial centre, first under Diocletian and then Maximian: Diocletian's constitutional reform between 286 and 293 divided the empire, and in 293 he added the commission of the Six Patricians, created specifically to conduct the prosecution of Carausius; in 296 the Caesar Constantius Chlorus crossed the sea with a combined army and fleet and recovered the whole island. On the imperial side the forces were the garrisons and auxiliary units of Gaul and the Rhine together with a navy that had to be rebuilt; on Carausius's side the backbone was the Channel fleet, manned in part by men recruited locally in Britain and by coastal auxiliaries, with Frankish and Saxon groups joining as raiding crews.
people: 卡勞修斯是整場叛亂的核心人物。他出身高盧北部的梅納皮人地區，在軍中歷任要職，終於取得海峽艦隊的指揮權；當馬克西米安對他提起貪污指控、準備派員審判之際，他沒有走上通往羅馬的道路，而是直接依靠手中艦隊與英國的駐軍自立為帝。他並非只求自保：其錢幣上留有「EXPECTAS VENI」（等待我來）的字樣，通常被解讀為他準備反攻高盧的宣言。他的財政官阿萊克圖斯後來在宮廷中將他殺死，奪位稱帝並維持統治約一年，成為英國史上第一位以弒君取得政權的僭主。收復全島的關鍵人物是當時的凱撒君士坦提烏斯·克洛魯斯：他在布洛涅集結海軍與陸軍，於296年登陸不列顛，在阿斯克勒庇俄多托斯（Asclepiodotum，一說在坎特伯雷附近）擊敗阿萊克圖斯，隨後逐漸控制南部、中部與北部；他回到羅馬只獲得 ovatio 的小凱旋，卻在306年被軍隊於約克推舉為奧古斯都，四個月後病逝，幼子君士坦丁隨即接位，開啟君士坦丁王朝。值得一提的還有卡勞修斯舊部阿斯克勒庇俄多托斯：他在打敗阿萊克圖斯之後赴羅馬報功，獲賜凱旋榮譽並取得執政官銜。
peopleEn: Carausius is the central figure of the whole rebellion. He came from the Menapian region of northern Gaul, held a series of important commands in the army, and finally obtained command of the Channel fleet; when Maximian brought an accusation of embezzlement against him and prepared to send judges to try him, he did not take the road to Rome but simply stood up as emperor on the strength of his fleet and the British garrisons. He was not merely acting in self-defence: his coins carry the legend EXPECTAS VENI, usually read as a declaration that he intended to invade Gaul. His finance minister, Allectus, later killed him in the palace and ruled for about a year in his place, becoming the first usurper in British history to seize power by murdering a Roman emperor. The decisive figure in the reconquest was the then Caesar, Constantius Chlorus: he assembled a fleet and an army at Gesoriacum, landed in Britain in 296, defeated Allectus at Asclepiodotum (thought to be near Canterbury), and then gradually took control of the south, the Midlands and the north. He was granted only an ovatio, a lesser triumph, when he returned to Rome, yet in 306 the army acclaimed him Augustus at York; he died four months later, and his young son Constantine succeeded him, opening the Constantinian dynasty. Another name worth recording is Asclepiodotus, an old adherent of Carausius: after defeating Allectus he travelled to Rome to claim his reward and was granted the honour of a triumph and the rank of consul.
kits: 卡面這件投石機（Onager）正是羅馬攻城體系的骨幹。公元前三世紀已見使用，是羅馬工程兵以絞盤的扭力把拋臂拉緊、靠蓄積的彈性勢能擲出石彈的攻城武器，射程可達數百步，主要用於打擊城牆、塔樓與堡壘的牆體，在圍城戰中取代撞錘而成為第一波破壞力。卡勞修斯之亂的兩端都離不開它：卡勞修斯一方可用投石機攻擊沿海的羅馬要塞與英格蘭西岸的防禦設施，296年的收復戰中，帝國的工程兵同樣要用它去啃薩克森海岸那些方石砌成的海岸堡壘。除了投石機，羅馬圍城還有各型弩砲（scorpio 與 ballista）、撞錘、攻城塔與帶射孔的攻城塔；守城一方則有弓弩、投石、滾木與從城頭反擲的配重石。海上更見關鍵：卡勞修斯的實力來自海峽艦隊，船上備有接舷用的長杆與登船用的軟梯，另有合乎潮流的快速帆船；帝國遠征軍的致命短板正是缺乏熟悉海峽潮流的舵手與水手，陸上再精銳也難以施展。裝備細節上，羅馬步兵仍以短劍、標槍與大橢圓盾為主，軍團以鷹旗與各軍旗維持陣形，工程兵則以斧、鎬、撬棍與繩梯在圍城線上作業。
kitsEn: The onager shown on the card is the backbone of the Roman siege system. It was already in use by the third century BC, and it is the siege weapon by which Roman engineers wound a torsion frame tight and converted the stored elastic energy of the throwing arm into a stone: its range ran to several hundred paces, and it was used to strike walls, towers and the fabric of strongholds, replacing the ram as the first wave of destruction in a siege. The Carausian rising needs the machine on both of its sides: Carausius could use it against the Roman coastal forts and the defences of the west coast of England, and in the reconquest of 296 the imperial engineers needed it to chew at the Saxon Shore forts built of squared stone. Alongside the onager the Roman siege train included the smaller bolt-throwers (scorpio and ballista), rams, and siege towers with firing slots; the defenders replied with bows, thrown stones, rolling logs and counterweights dropped from the parapets. At sea the stakes were even higher: Carausius's strength was the Channel fleet, fitted with long boarding poles and scaling ladders, together with fast sailing craft that could work the tides; the gravest weakness of the imperial expeditionary force was the lack of pilots and crews who knew the Channel, and no amount of infantry excellence could compensate. In terms of personal equipment the Roman infantry still fought with the short sword, the throwing javelin and the large oval shield, the legions kept their formations together with the eagle and the standards of the individual units, and the engineers worked along the siege line with axes, picks, crowbars and rope ladders.
tactics: 整場衝突的勝負手在海峽，而不在陸上的陣線。卡勞修斯起義之初便控制了艦隊基地與英國的補給港口，等於捏住羅馬西部的海運命脈；帝國遠征軍每次都得從高盧集結船隊跨海登陸，距離雖短，但潮流多變、風向不定的英吉利海峽對不熟悉的水手極不友善，289年第一次遠征的海軍在風暴中全滅，290年馬克西米安親率大軍再攻，仍因無法讓船隊安全通過海峽而無功而返。卡勞修斯一方則以艦隊巡弋、封鎖航線、切斷英國與大陸的往來為主要戰法，海盜出身的快速船隻既是騷擾的工具，也是徵募兵源與財貨的來源。296年的收復戰中，康斯坦提烏斯吸取教訓，先確保制海權：以海軍掩護運輸船隊，選擇英國東岸、接近河口與港口的地點登陸，陸軍隨即在阿斯克勒庇俄多托斯一役中與阿萊克圖斯的部隊決戰，取勝後迅速推進至倫敦與泰晤士河谷，再以工程兵配投石機強攻沿線的薩克森海岸堡壘，最後逐段向北肅清殘餘據點。守方的野外部隊與堡壘中的防禦相結合，而整場戰役拖得最久的關鍵，始終是海上補給線究竟落在哪一方的手中。
tacticsEn: The whole conflict was decided in the Channel, not on any line of battle on land. Carausius seized the fleet bases and the supply ports of Britain at the very beginning of the revolt, which meant holding the sea arteries of the western empire in his fist. Every imperial expedition had to assemble shipping in Gaul and cross the sea; the distance was short, but the Channel, with its shifting tides and unreliable winds, was merciless to crews who did not know it, and in 289 the fleet of the first expedition was destroyed in a storm. In 290 Maximian himself led a second attempt in person and again achieved nothing, because he could not get his ships safely through the Channel. Carausius's side fought mainly by cruising with the fleet, closing the sea routes and cutting Britain off from the continent, while the fast boats of the pirates served both as a means of harassment and as a source of recruits and plunder. In the reconquest of 296 Constantius had learned the lesson and secured the command of the sea first: the fleet covered the transports, the troops were put ashore on the east coast of Britain near estuaries and harbours, and the army then fought Allectus's force in the battle of Asclepiodotum. From there it advanced rapidly on London and the Thames valley, stormed the Saxon Shore forts along the line with engineers and onagers, and finally swept the remaining strongholds out of the north one sector at a time. The defenders combined field troops with the resistance of the forts themselves, but the thing that prolonged the campaign was always the same: which side's hand held the sea supply line.
data: 時間軸上，卡勞修斯通常被記為公元286年冬至287年初舉兵，執政至293年前後被阿萊克圖斯刺殺；阿萊克圖斯稱帝約一年，296年在阿斯克勒庇俄多托斯兵敗身亡；同年康斯坦提烏斯收復不列顛，306年4月被軍隊於約克推為奧古斯都，7月4日病逝於約克。分離的時間約七年，是羅馬帝國西部行省中一次為時最長的脫離。與之相關的數字還有：293年戴克里先設立的「六貴族」委員會人數為六，正是為追訴卡勞修斯而設；卡勞修斯鑄造的貨幣流通約七年，錢幣上多見「EXPECTAS VENI」字樣與戰艦圖樣，並有「CARAUSIUS ET ALLECTVS」的聯名幣，其鑄幣作坊的具體位置學界尚有爭議，一般認為在倫敦一帶；英格蘭東南的薩克森海岸防線由十座左右的方石堡壘組成，考古發掘顯示佩恩西的 Portus Adurni 與 Othona 一帶的工事始於卡勞修斯時期，即在叛亂期間就已加築。海峽艦隊的主要基地為布洛涅與諾維奧杜努姆兩處，而英格蘭與高盧北岸之間的定期航線，恰恰落在叛軍控制之中。
dataEn: On the chronology, Carausius is usually recorded as rising at the end of AD 286 or in the early months of 287, and as ruling until about 293, when Allectus murdered him; Allectus then ruled for about a year and was killed after his defeat at Asclepiodotum in 296; in the same year Constantius recovered Britain, and in April 306 the army acclaimed him Augustus at York, where he died on 4 July. The separation lasted about seven years, the longest such break-away in the western provinces of the Roman Empire. Other figures that belong to the episode are these: the commission of the Six Patricians set up by Diocletian in 293 numbered six men and existed precisely to prosecute Carausius; the coinage struck by Carausius circulated for roughly seven years, most of the pieces carrying the legend EXPECTAS VENI and an image of a warship, and there exist joint issues reading CARAUSIUS ET ALLECTVS, while the position of the mint that produced them is still disputed, most scholars placing it in the neighbourhood of London; the Saxon Shore line on the south-east coast of England was made up of something like ten squared-stone forts, and excavation has shown that the works at Portus Adurni near Pegnsey and at Othona were begun in Carausius's own time, that is, they were added to during the revolt. The main bases of the Channel fleet were two, Gesoriacum and Noviodunum, and the regular shipping lines between Britain and the north coast of Gaul lay precisely in the hands of the rebels.
cause: 導火索是一道貪污指控，但根子仍在帝國邊防體系的結構性脆弱。卡勞修斯奉命以海峽艦隊清剿法蘭克與撒克遜海盜；沿海各省屢遭劫掠，朝廷卻沒有能力根除這批來去如潮的掠奪者，於是流傳出「放縱海盜、坐收贓物」的說法，指控他故意縱敵並私吞掠奪所得。馬克西米安準備派員前往審問，而擺在卡勞修斯面前的現實是：他一旦受審，就等於交出艦隊，交出英國的兵源與稅源，交出自己經營多年的一切。戴克里先的改革又把整個體制重新洗牌，分權四帝、新設禁衛軍總監與高級官職、六貴族委員會，把原本集中在元老與將領手上的裁量權切得更碎，這使身處關鍵位置的軍官既有了向上鑽營的空間，也有了獨立的資本。於是一名掌握戰略海峽的邊軍統帥，發現自保的代價不過是自稱皇帝，便選擇了自稱皇帝。更深一層的原因是三世紀羅馬的軍隊政治：駐軍可以推舉皇帝，邊疆的實際控制往往比中央的文書更有力量。
causeEn: The trigger was a charge of embezzlement, but the root of it lay in the structural weakness of the imperial frontier system. Carausius was ordered to use the Channel fleet against Frankish and Saxon pirates; the coastal provinces were repeatedly plundered, and the government had no means of destroying this tide that came and went, so the story went out that he let the pirates loose and pocketed the proceeds, deliberately sparing them. Maximian prepared to send judges across the Channel, and the reality facing Carausius was this: if he submitted to trial he would hand over the fleet, the sources of manning and tax in Britain, and everything he had built. Diocletian's reforms then reshuffled the whole structure, dividing the empire among four emperors, adding the praetorian prefectures and the higher offices, and creating the commission of the Six Patricians, breaking the discretionary power that had rested with the Senate and the generals into still smaller pieces; for an officer standing at a point of strategic importance this created room to climb and capital of his own. A commander of a frontier army who held the strategic Channel therefore found that the price of his own security was the simple business of calling himself emperor, and he called himself emperor. One layer deeper lies the military politics of the third-century empire: garrisons made emperors, and effective control of a frontier was very often a truer fact than the documents of the centre.
impact: 其一是英格蘭在政治上脫離帝國七年。這段期間島上另鑄貨幣、另設官署，帝國的稅收、軍糧與軍團輪調在英格蘭全部中斷，直到296年才重新接上，也迫使帝國在島上重建一套能運作的行政與駐軍體系。其二是推動了帝國最高層的機構改革：戴克里先的分權、禁衛軍總監的設立與六貴族委員會的組建，最高官制的調整多有與如何處置卡勞修斯這一課直接相關。其三是重塑了海防：薩克森海岸的堡壘網在叛亂期間加築、在收復之後擴建，帝國重新取得海峽的制海權，並把海峽艦隊與沿海基地視為不可分割的戰略資產，此後數百年的「守海岸」戰略由此定型。其四是留下了一種政治範式：在帝國本土以外自立為帝，用地方稅收維持軍隊，靠鑄幣宣示合法性，這套做法在四世紀末至五世紀初的不列顛再度出現，成為後世所說的「不列顛僭主」的雛型。
impactEn: First, England was politically separated from the empire for seven years. In that time the island struck its own coinage and set up its own offices, and the taxes, military grain and rotation of legions that Britain owed the empire were interrupted altogether until the link was restored in 296; the empire was likewise obliged to rebuild on the island an administrative and garrison system that could actually work. Second, the episode pushed forward the reform of the highest imperial offices: the division of the empire among four rulers, the setting up of the praetorian prefectures, and the commission of the Six Patricians all have much to do with the lessons of how Carausius was to be handled. Third, it reshaped the maritime defence: the network of forts along the Saxon Shore was enlarged during the revolt and expanded after the reconquest, the empire recovered the command of the Channel, and the Channel fleet and the coastal bases came to be treated as one indivisible strategic asset, fixing the shape of the coastal-defence strategy for the centuries that followed. Fourth, it left behind a political model: to make oneself emperor outside the imperial core, to maintain an army from local taxes, and to proclaim legitimacy by striking coin; the same expedient reappeared in Britain in the late fourth and early fifth centuries and became the prototype of the British usurpers.
result: 結果是分裂以軍事收復告終，而不是以談判或承認告終。卡勞修斯本人死於宮廷政變，殺他的是自己的財政官阿萊克圖斯；阿萊克圖斯又在一場由東岸向倫敦推進的戰役中敗於康斯坦提烏斯，並被卡勞修斯舊部阿斯克勒庇俄多托斯所殺。收復之後，帝國沒有把英格蘭當作可以放手的地方：不列顛重新設總督，重整軍團編制，修築薩克森海岸的堡壘，並把英國的稅收與物資重新納入帝國的預算；康斯坦提烏斯因此在306年獲軍隊推舉為奧古斯都，他一死，其子君士坦丁於307年接位，開啟延續半個多世紀的君士坦丁王朝。但真正的結果並不只是一位皇帝之死：這場叛亂證明了兩件事，一是掌握海峽艦隊的人足以自立為帝，二是帝國只要無法在一年之內把海峽的控制權收回來，島嶼就會淪為另一個政治中心。
resultEn: The outcome was a military reconquest, not a negotiation or a recognition. Carausius himself died in a palace coup, murdered by his own finance minister Allectus; Allectus in turn was defeated by Constantius in a campaign advancing from the east coast towards London and was killed by Asclepiodotus, an old adherent of Carausius. After the reconquest the empire did not treat England as a place it could afford to let go: Britain again had a governor, the legionary organisation was put back in order, the forts of the Saxon Shore were repaired, and Britain's taxes and supplies were returned to the imperial budget. Constantius was accordingly acclaimed Augustus by the army in 306; when he died his son Constantine succeeded him in 307, opening a dynasty that lasted more than half a century. Yet the true result is not the death of an emperor: the rebellion proved two things. That a man who held the Channel fleet was strong enough to make himself emperor, and that if the empire could not recover command of the Channel within a year, the island would become a separate centre of power in its own right.
